title: MRI from magnetic-resonance gradients to practical clinical imaging
pressure: X-ray/CT exposed ionizing radiation and had tissue-contrast limits; NMR encoded tissue chemistry but lacked useful spatial localization.
preExistingWorldModel: NMR spectroscopy was mature for chemical samples; large magnets, gradients, computation and reconstruction for whole-body imaging remained difficult.
observationsAndInstruments: Lauterbur introduced magnetic-field gradients and 2-D imaging in 1973.
Mansfield developed mathematical/gradient methods improving localization and speed.
Human scanners integrated larger magnets, RF coils and reconstruction computers.
MRI gained clinical value particularly in soft tissue without ionizing radiation.
decisiveTests: reconstruct distinguishable structures from resonance signals
make whole-body magnets/RF safe and reliable in hospitals
technicalOrScientificTransition: Spatial encoding opened the imaging frontier, while practical MRI required magnet, gradient, RF, computing and clinical workflow engineering.
rivalsAndFailures: Proof-of-principle images were far from a hospital scanner.
CT remained superior for some tasks.
Higher fields create engineering/safety/artifact tradeoffs as well as signal benefits.
diffusionAndScaling: Diffusion depended on complements, cost/yield/standards and institutional adoption; the nominal breakthrough date did not equal broad effective use.
standardsAndInstitutions: Laboratories, firms, standard bodies, regulators, users and infrastructure operators owned different parts of evidence, implementation and consequence.
externalitiesAndCorrections: Lifecycle harms and authority changes are preserved where evidenced rather than inferred from local technical success.
secondOrderEffects: Spatial encoding opened the imaging frontier, while practical MRI required magnet, gradient, RF, computing and clinical workflow engineering.
sourceNativeSummary: Spatial encoding opened the imaging frontier, while practical MRI required magnet, gradient, RF, computing and clinical workflow engineering.
unresolvedHistoricalQuestions: Which complement most constrained diffusion at each lifecycle phase?
Which later narrative compresses materially distributed work?
